audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) The page says 'sidestep his E pull' as if Nevermove roots on the way out — Riot's text is that the wave travels forward, then RETURNS and roots what it hits, so the return pass is the dangerous one. (2) Vision of Empire (W) reveals champions it hits, which hard-counters Akshan's Going Rogue camouflage. That interaction is absent from both layers and it is the one thing that stops the Akshan map game.
audit.why: Riot description of Nevermove: 'launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' Riot description of Vision of Empire: 'Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment.' Akshan's W is camouflage, which reveal breaks.
audit.corrected: Nevermove (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) roots on the return pass — dodge after it flies past. Vision of Empire (W) reveals, so it strips Going Rogue camouflage and feeds him a Soul Fragment.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'For its whole cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1. The whole matchup is the gap between his pulls, so the number is the advice.

Ravenous Flock (P) heals off every Soul Fragment and permanently raises his max health; Demonic Ascension is indefinite while draining champions. Grievous Wounds is the item decision this matchup turns on.

edits.before: Swain is one of the easiest level-1s to disrespect: his Q (Death's Hand) cone is short-ranged and his E (Nevermove) pull-root is his only real threat, so the whole early game is sidestepping that one skillshot. Dodge his E and he is defenseless: walk up, throw Q for the boomerang chip, and let your passive's second shot stack the bonus-magic proc and shield onto you. Don't stand in a straight line at minion range or he'll land E, root you, and W-bomb you for a real chunk — but if that pull whiffs, he has nothing for its whole cooldown.
edits.after: Swain is one of the easiest level-1s to disrespect: his Q (Death's Hand) reaches 750 and his E (Nevermove) is his only real threat, so the early game is dodging one skillshot twice. Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the way out — sidestep after it has flown past you. Dodge it and he is defenceless for 12s: walk up, throw Q for the boomerang chip, and let your passive's second shot stack the magic proc and shield onto you. Never stand in a line at minion range, or the root lands and Vision of Empire (W) drops on top of it.

edits.before: Land E (Nevermove) to pull and root you, then chain W bomb so you can't kite or swing away
edits.after: Root you on the Nevermove (E) return pass, then drop Vision of Empire (W) where you can't walk out

edits.before: Stack R soul fragments and drag you into a long AOE drain fight where his sustain beats your short trades
edits.after: Reveal your Going Rogue (W) camo with Vision of Empire, then drag you into a long drain fight he wins

edits.before: E (Heroic Swing) gives you a poke-and-escape his immobile kit can't answer — chip him every time his E pull is on cooldown.
edits.after: E (Heroic Swing) is a poke-and-escape his immobile kit cannot answer — chip him through every one of Nevermove's 12 down seconds.

edits.before: His one kill threat is a landed E (Nevermove) pull that roots you next to him into W bomb and R drain — eat that chain at melee range and a winning trade flips into your death.
edits.after: His one kill threat is Nevermove (E) rooting you on its return pass, straight into Vision of Empire (W) and the R drain — eat that chain in melee and a winning trade flips into your death.

edits.before: You own the lane through your first lethality item, but Swain is a hard scaler — once he hits 2+ items his R drain makes him tanky while his AP burst climbs and your lethality falls off. A landed E (Nevermove) into W bomb with R draining will delete a squishy, low-resist Akshan in any extended fight. Close it out before then: snowball your early lead with E-reset swings, take plates and lane priority, and let your team peel a full-build Swain in teamfights rather than dueling him at 25+ minutes.
edits.after: You own the lane through your first lethality item, but Swain is a hard scaler — once he hits 2+ items his R drain makes him tanky while his AP burst climbs and your lethality falls off. Ravenous Flock (P) heals him off every Soul Fragment and permanently grows his health bar, so Grievous Wounds is what keeps your chip meaningful past 20 minutes. Close it out before then: snowball your early lead with E-reset swings, take plates and lane priority, and let your team peel a full-build Swain rather than dueling him.

notes: The reveal on Vision of Empire is the single most important thing this page was missing — it is the counter to Going Rogue camouflage and to Akshan's roam game, and neither layer mentioned it. Also corrected the Nevermove root to the return pass and added its 12s cooldown.
